_about: Parameters of the behaviour layer's segments and features (agentcake/detect/segment.py and features.py). The values are our lab's, unchanged (the behaviour lab's labcore.py, 2026-11-11); the missing-data variant is our PostHog study's (cake-ph-eval/phcore.py, 2026-11-12); no_focus_events, hover_after_scroll_ms, offset_tolerance_px and window_geo_ms narrow three features for 0.6.2, and untrusted_events the untrusted one (the features section says why).

segments._about: window_ms: length of the fixed windows. One segment per action: events of a typing or scroll burst are at most gap_ms apart; pointer moves within scroll_move_ms of a scroll burst belong to it (moves made while scrolling); a pause longer than approach_pause_ms between pointer moves ends the approach to the next action.

features._about: min_duration_s: shortest segment length for move_rate. before_click_ms, hover_ms, down_ms: how far before a click to look for mouse moves, a mouseover on the same target and the mousedown. min_path_moves: trusted moves needed for the path features; cv_min_speeds and jerk_min_speeds: speeds needed for speed_cv and jerk_any; jerk_speed_step: a speed change above this (px/ms) is a jerk. wheel_after_ms: a scroll this soon after a wheel or key event came from it, as does one while a finger or a button is held down or this soon after its release (after agent-detector's scroll drivers, MIT). keydown_before_ms: typed text this soon after a keydown came from it. typed_input_types: the input types that are typed text, the only ones input_no_keydown reads (after agent-detector's insertWithoutKeys, MIT): a paste, an autofill or a correction (insertReplacementText), a drop and an input method's composition (isComposing) change a field without a keydown, and humans make them; nor does it read a session where a finger or a pen gave input. metronome_min_keys and burst_min_keys: keydowns needed for key_iv_cv and key_burst; key_burst_ms: keydowns closer than this are a burst. click_lt_px: a click closer than this to the centre of its target. offset_min_events: pointer events with screen positions needed on the page for screen_offset_jump. screen_eq_min_positions: screen_eq_client counts screen positions equal to page positions only when they were equal at this many different places in the session (after bot-signal's cdp-input-coordinate-leak, MIT): one place is a window in the screen's corner. double_click_box_px: a mouse click repeats the previous mouse click in place when it lands inside the square of this side centred on that click and every mousemove between the two stayed inside it too: the square within which a browser counts a second click as one at the same place (Chromium's MouseEvent::IsRepeatedClickEvent: 4 by 4 px, Windows' default double-click rectangle, SM_CXDOUBLECLK by SM_CYDOUBLECLK). Such a click shows no approach of its own, the pointer being on the spot already: a person paging through pictures or pressing a calendar's arrow again, an agent pressing a button twice, a label passing its click to its input. So moves_before_click leaves it out, as do the teleport clicks and the timeline's pointer features (behavior_model.json); where it lands on its target (the click centre features) is still read. No time limit: however long the pointer rests on the spot, it makes no new approach. Narrowed for 0.6.2 after a person was taken for an agent (11/24: someone scrolled and hovered the browser beside their editor). no_focus_events: the events no_focus reads, the ones a person makes only in a window that has focus: a click, a key, and of the inputs only typed text (typed_input_types, not an input method's composition), since the keyboard goes to the active window alone. On a Mac a person scrolls and moves the pointer over a window that is not active, and drops or pastes into one from its menu, so those are left out; an agent that drives the browser through its debugging protocol clicks and types in a window without focus (Claude Code driving Claude in Chrome while its user works in a terminal). hover_after_scroll_ms: a mousemove or pointermove that reports no movement where the pointer already was, at most this long after a wheel or a scroll, is the browser telling the page what is under a pointer that rests while the page scrolls, so zero_movement_frac leaves it out: measured with Playwright's WebKit 27.2 (Safari's engine), 85 to 100 ms after each wheel scroll; Chromium 149 and Firefox 157 send none. offset_tolerance_px: screen_offset_jump counts a change of the screen-minus-client offset only beyond this many pixels on either axis (a page zoomed from 100% shifts the offset a little as the pointer moves). A change is the window's, not a jump, when cake.js's geometry records show the window moving by it (within the tolerance) between the pointer event before and window_geo_ms after the press (cake.js records the window's place every 500 ms, cakejs.json raw.geo_poll_ms, so a move shows in its records up to that long later), or when the next mousemove keeps the new offset: the page's place on the screen moved (a window dragged, DevTools opened beside the page), while a script's press differs from the pointer events on both sides of it. A click the keyboard made (detail 0) has no pointer position: Chromium 149 and Firefox 157 give it 0 for every position (measured), so it is neither a press nor the event before one. untrusted_events: the events a script dispatched (isTrusted false) that the untrusted feature counts, the ones that report a device: a button, a key, the pointer, the wheel or a finger. A page's own scripts dispatch clicks, inputs and changes (a carousel that turns itself with element.click(), a widget that sets a field, a framework's trigger) while a person sits still, as agents' scripts do, so those are left out of untrusted, and every feature that reads the visitor's input reads only the events their own devices made (features.py visitor_input). After agent-detector 0.4.1 (MIT, github.com/doubleagent-so/agent-detector a523214c3b67): it counts untrusted pointer downs, keys and pointer moves only, and reads no behaviour from untrusted events; its check of fields a script set ships as a shadow signal, weighted 0. The releases (mouseup, pointerup, keyup) and the wheel and touch events are the same devices' events: in our recordings of agents, Selenium driven over MCP dispatched untrusted mouseups and Antigravity untrusted wheels. Narrowed for 0.6.2.

unobservable._about: Features an rrweb-only recording cannot measure (no keydown, no wheel, no screenX/Y, no movementX/Y). Without raw input they are null (no data), never 0: the missing-data variant.
